name: Dense operator console
feel: Linear / Datadog energy: a tool for people who live in it eight hours a day. Dark, compact, keyboard-first, numbers in monospace, every pixel earns its place.
structure: Icon rail or narrow sidebar, a command palette hint in the topbar, one dominant data region (table, status board or log), inspector panel on the right. Dense 32px rows, sticky headers, filters inline.
neutrals: near-black canvas with a faint blue-grey or green-grey tint, surfaces one step lighter, hairline borders
do: tabular numerals everywhere
keyboard shortcuts shown next to actions
status as coloured dot + text
monospace for ids, timestamps and values

name: Editorial workspace
feel: A well-set magazine turned into a product: warm paper neutrals, a serif display face for titles, generous margins, content first and chrome almost invisible.
structure: Thin top bar, wide centred content column (max 960px) with a quiet left index or table of contents, actions as text links or small ghost buttons. Few borders: hierarchy comes from type scale and spacing.
neutrals: warm off-white canvas (cream, bone), ink-black text, borders as light warm grey rules
do: serif for headings, humanist sans (Source Sans 3 or Alegreya Sans) for body and UI
large type scale: 32 / 20 / 15 / 13
rules and whitespace instead of boxes
one accent used for links and the primary action only

name: Soft product
feel: Stripe / Vercel daylight: cool white, soft shadows, pill controls, friendly and precise. The default of good SaaS, done with care rather than by habit.
structure: Left sidebar with grouped nav, page header with title + primary button, content as a few large panels (not a grid of small cards), tables with generous 44px rows.
neutrals: cool white canvas, pure white surfaces with a soft 1px border and a faint shadow, text in deep navy-grey rather than black
do: one soft shadow scale (sm / md), used sparingly
pill-shaped inputs and buttons
accent used on the primary button, links, active nav and focus rings
icons at 16px with 1.5px stroke
dont: no slate/grey-blue Tailwind defaults, tint the neutrals toward the accent
no more than one shadow level per view
no outlined cards stacked in a 4-column grid

name: Brutalist grid
feel: Visible structure: 1px solid black borders, square corners, big type, offset blocks and raw labels. Confident, a bit rude, extremely legible.
structure: Full-width grid where every region is a bordered cell. Topbar as a thick black band or a bordered row. Tables with heavy header, lists with numbered rows, actions as bordered boxes.
neutrals: off-white or pale canvas, pure black text and borders, one bold accent block
do: borders 1-2px solid, no shadows
uppercase monospace labels for metadata
hover states as inversion (black bg, white text)
accent as a filled block, not a tint

name: Terminal
feel: A modern TUI in the browser: monospace everywhere, phosphor accent, lines and brackets as structure. For logs, pipelines, devops, anything an engineer watches.
structure: Full-width stacked panes with single-line headers (`── name ──`), a status line at the bottom, a log or table as the dominant region, side pane as a tree or key/value list.
neutrals: true dark canvas (#0b0e0c family), panes separated by 1px lines or dim box characters, dim grey for secondary text
do: one monospace family for everything, including headings
status in bracketed tokens like [ OK ] [FAIL]
keyboard hints in the status line
accent for the cursor, active row and primary values only
dont: no icons except small inline glyphs
no more than one accent plus red for errors

name: Analytics board
feel: Charts lead, chrome recedes: a KPI band with big tabular numerals, then two or three large charts. Muted neutrals, one accent, a disciplined 3-tone chart palette.
structure: Compact topbar with a date-range control, KPI band of 4-6 tiles with sparklines, then a 2/3 + 1/3 chart row, then a table or ranked list. No left sidebar, or a collapsed icon rail.
neutrals: quiet neutral canvas with a faint tint, surfaces nearly flat, hairline borders, chart grid lines very dim
do: numbers 28-40px, tabular, with unit and delta
charts drawn as inline SVG with axis labels and units
accent + two neutral tones for series, red/green only for deltas
legend inline, not a floating box
dont: no card per tiny metric in a 6-column grid

name: Glass dark
feel: Liquid-glass night mode: deep gradient canvas, translucent blurred surfaces, soft glows on the accent, large radii. Premium feel for consumer-facing or showcase apps.
structure: Floating panels over the canvas with 16-24px gaps, a floating top pill nav or left glass rail, one hero panel (map, media, main object) with smaller glass tiles around it.
neutrals: deep canvas gradient (navy-black, plum-black or green-black), surfaces white at 6-10% opacity with backdrop blur and a 1px white/10 border
do: backdrop-blur on every surface, with a subtle inner highlight
accent glow (box-shadow with accent at 30%) on the primary action only
text white at 92% / 60% for hierarchy
keep body text at 4.5:1 on the blurred surface
dont: no text on busy gradients without a surface behind

name: Warm craft
feel: Human and tactile: cream canvas, earthy accents (terracotta, olive, mustard), rounded but not bubbly, soft tinted surfaces instead of borders. For wellness, education, community, small-business tools.
structure: Top nav with the brand on the left, content in a two-column arrangement (main + a warm-tinted side column), lists as rounded rows with avatars, forms with large labelled fields.
neutrals: cream canvas, surfaces slightly whiter or slightly darker cream, borders rare and warm, text in dark brown-black
do: tinted surfaces (accent at 8-12%) to group content instead of borders
friendly microcopy with real names and places
tags as soft pills with tinted backgrounds
icons rounded, 20px
dont: no pure white or pure black
no dense tables; use lists or cards with 3-4 fields

name: Swiss grid
feel: International typographic style: strict 12-column grid, strong type scale, black on white, one primary accent, rules as separators and nothing decorative. Timeless, authoritative.
structure: Top bar as a single rule with text nav, generous left margin with section labels, content aligned to the grid, tables with top rule only, actions as text in uppercase or small solid rectangles.
neutrals: pure white canvas, black text, mid-grey (4.5:1) for secondary, 1px black or light-grey rules
do: type scale 48 / 24 / 16 / 12, tight leading on headings
left-align everything, no centred text
accent on at most two elements per screen
grid gutters visible through alignment, never through boxes
dont: no icons where a word works

name: Bento tiles
feel: Modular tile mosaic: a grid of tiles of mixed sizes (1x1, 2x1, 2x2), each a self-contained mini-view with its own title and one strong element. Playful but orderly.
structure: Compact header, then a CSS grid of 12 columns with tiles spanning 3/4/6/8 columns and 1-2 rows. The most important object gets the 2x2 tile at the top-left. No sidebar.
neutrals: quiet canvas, tiles one step lighter (light) or darker (dark), 1px border, 16px gap
do: each tile has a small caps title and ONE dominant element (number, chart, list, image)
tile sizes follow importance
one or two tiles tinted with the accent at 10-15%
consistent 20px padding in every tile
dont: no uniform 4x N grid of same-size cards
no tile with more than three sub-sections
no gradients across the whole canvas

name: Industrial HMI
feel: Control-room grade: dark grey panels, big touch-safe targets, gauges and state lights with unambiguous colours, grouped panels with labelled headers. Built for monitoring and devices.
structure: Full-width top status band (system state, alarms, time), a main synoptic or device grid, a right alarm list, bottom quick actions as large buttons. Panels with a 28px header strip.
neutrals: graphite canvas, panels one step lighter with a 2px darker border, text off-white, labels in uppercase grey
do: minimum 40px targets
state colours fixed: green run, amber warn, red alarm, grey off, always with text
semi-condensed face for dense labels
gauges and bars drawn as inline SVG with ticks and units
dont: no thin 1px lines for critical separations

name: Paper ledger
feel: Back-office done right: forms and tables dominate, zebra rows, left-aligned labels, quiet green-grey neutrals, everything reachable by keyboard. Looks like a tool an accountant trusts.
structure: Sidebar with text nav grouped by module, breadcrumb + page title, a filter bar, a full-width table with 36px rows and a right-aligned numeric column set, a detail drawer for editing.
neutrals: pale green-grey or warm-grey canvas, white surfaces, 1px cool-grey borders, text near-black
do: zebra rows and right-aligned tabular numbers
labels above or left of fields, 13px, consistent widths
totals row sticky at the bottom
primary action in the page header only
dont: no KPI card row on top of a table
no icon-only actions in rows without tooltips

name: Neon arcade
feel: Synthwave night arcade: dark canvas, electric multi-colour accents, glow, scorelines and big numbers. References: synthwave posters, arcade cabinet UIs, retro racing HUDs.
structure: Full-bleed dark app shell with a top score/level band, a central play panel, and side tiles for lives, timer, rewards; on mobile it collapses to a top HUD, one large action zone, and a bottom swipe rail.
neutrals: near-black indigo or black canvas, dark slate surfaces, white text, thin neon edge highlights
do: use 2-4px neon borders and soft glow shadows on primary actions only
layer multiple accent hues for score, timer, lives, and progress
use big display numerals for score, streak, and countdown
add subtle scanlines, grid floors, or CRT flicker as background texture
dont: no beige neutrals or muted greys
no dense tables or dashboard charts
no blur-heavy glass if it hides the HUD

name: Sticker pop
feel: Friendly sticker-book consumer app: bright flat colour fields, thick rounded shapes, chunky 3D-ish buttons with a hard bottom shadow, and a mascot slot. References: Duolingo, Headspace, Nintendo mobile UIs.
structure: Light rounded app shell with a top brand row, a large hero card for the main task, stacked rounded cards for modes and progress, and a bottom tab bar on mobile.
neutrals: warm white canvas, cream or pale pastel panels, near-black text, saturated accent blocks
do: use 3-6px hard bottom shadows on buttons and cards, not soft blur
fill large rounded panels with saturated hue blocks
reserve one mascot or illustration slot for the hero
use rounded type for headings and friendly microcopy
dont: no sharp corners on primary surfaces

name: 8-bit game UI
feel: Retro 8/16-bit game screen: pixel font titles, hard 2-4px borders, square corners, dithered or flat panels, HP bars, coin counters, and dialog boxes. References: NES, Game Boy, and CGA-era game menus.
structure: Square-cornered game shell with a top status bar for HP, coins, and level, a central dialog box or play field, and bottom action buttons; on mobile it becomes a full-width status band, one main panel, and thumb-reachable buttons.
neutrals: flat black, white, grey, or Game Boy olive-green surfaces, with hard black or white borders
do: use 2-4px solid borders and no anti-aliased soft shadows
keep palette limited to 4-6 flat colours per screen
use blocky progress bars, coin counters, and dialog boxes
use pixel fonts for titles and body only when legible at size
dont: no more than one accent colour per panel

name: Comic zine pop
feel: Comic / zine brutal-pop: thick black outlines, halftone or diagonal hatch fills, bold condensed display, speech-bubble callouts, tilted stickers and tags. References: pop-comic posters, indie zines, and comic book HUDs.
structure: Off-white or black comic shell with a masthead band, a main panel framed by thick black borders, side callout bubbles, and a bottom action strip; on mobile it stacks into a title panel, one large action panel, and a tab bar.
neutrals: off-white paper or black ink canvas, pure black outlines, white highlights, one high-saturation fill
do: use 3-6px black outlines on panels, buttons, and stickers
apply halftone dots or diagonal hatches as fills, not full-surface noise
use speech-bubble callouts for tips, errors, and rewards
tilt secondary stickers and tags by 2-6 degrees
dont: no rounded pill buttons without outlines
no busy backgrounds behind body text
